_metadata.purpose: Maps common Kanuri security/fraud-related terms to their canonical English keyword equivalents, for use in multilingual scam/threat detection.
_metadata.disclaimer: IMPORTANT: this is the most minimal and lowest-confidence file in the set, more so even than fulfulde.json. Kanuri (Central Kanuri / Yerwa Kanuri, ISO 639-3: knc) is a Nilo-Saharan language, spoken mainly in Borno State, Nigeria and around Lake Chad. Unlike Hausa/Yoruba/Igbo/Fulfulde, it is NOT closely related to any of the other languages in this project, so no cross-language cognate inference was possible. After extensive searching, only ONE term (ndaltere/steal) could be confirmed against an academic source (the World Loanword Database, a Max Planck Institute publication). Everything else here is a common loanword assumption, not a sourced fact. This file should be treated as a placeholder more than a glossary, and needs native Kanuri-speaker input before any real reliance on it.

confidence_levels.verified: Cross-checked against a published academic source — for this file, only the World Loanword Database (Löhr & Wolff 2009).
confidence_levels.common: A loanword pattern consistent with regional contact (Hausa/English/Arabic all have historical contact with Kanuri); not independently confirmed this session.

notes: Kanuri historically absorbed vocabulary from Arabic (via Islamic scholarship, pre-modern period), Hausa (medieval-to-modern contact), and English/French (colonial and postcolonial period) — documented in the World Loanword Database's own contact-period chronology for this language. This makes English/Hausa-style loanwords for modern technical concepts a reasonable assumption, following the same pattern as Fulfulde.

No stopword list is included: no Kanuri grammatical/function words could be confirmed this session, and Kanuri's postposition-based, SOV grammar with noun-class agreement is different enough from the other five languages that guessing would be irresponsible without a source.

ndaltere.note: Confirmed via the World Loanword Database (Löhr & Wolff, 2009), a Max Planck Institute academic publication. Original form: ndàltə́.
